title: Reconstruction Topology Consolidation Review
purpose: Review MPF-RTOP-001 through MPF-RTOP-009 as a coherent embedded reconstruction-topology scaffold and determine whether the framework remains safe for continued analog-only exploration.
review_findings: Reconstruction neighborhoods successfully define mutual reconstructability limits without identity claims.
Accessibility relations are rigorously governed as directional and non-reversible.
Recoverability corridors provide stable transformation paths while preserving projection distinctions.
Deformation modes and risk classes effectively characterize topological distortion.
Conflict boundary preservation is enforced as a mandatory structural indicator.
Embedded observer constraints define necessary gaps in reconstruction accessibility.
Drift detection provides a linguistic firewall against topology-language escalation.
Stress tests confirm metric robustness against adversarial identity and unity assumptions.
remaining_risks: Directional accessibility may still be psychologically misread as symmetric equivalence.
Observer constraints are qualitative and dependent on complete participatory accounting.
Topological language requires continuous monitoring to prevent realism drift.
forbidden_next_steps: Claiming reconstruction topology proves source identity.
